chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf ibn Baqah, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Ibrahim ibn Umar who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The affair of Allah is totally strange (unknowable), however, He only holds you to account over that part which He has given you knowledge of about Himself.

key_terms.عَرَفَكُم: He made you know/He revealed to you

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between God's unknowable nature and human accountability according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the paradox of divine omnipotence and human accountability, asserting that while God's essence and decrees are ultimately wondrous and beyond full comprehension, He does not burden souls with the unknown. This principle, central to Shia theological epistemology, emphasizes that divine justice relies on the clear self-disclosure (tanzil) of God through prophets and signs, ensuring that human responsibility is grounded in accessible revelation rather than hidden mysteries.
